newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Short Australian debt unnerved by falling A$.
newsitem.headline: Short Australian debt unnerved by falling A$.

text.p: *Short-dated Australian debt futures were under pressure as continued weakness in the local dollar unsettled hopes of a further easing in monetary policy.
*Westpac consumer sentiment survey at 2.30 p.m. (0430 GMT).
Short-dated Australian debt futures remained under pressure at midday on Wednesday as continued weakness in the Australian dollar unsettled hopes of a further easing in monetary policy.

The local currency sank to a fresh 18-month of around US$0.7310/15 and was close to testing key support at the 1996 low of US$0.7305, while the September bill contract slid nine basis points at one stage to a low of 94.77.
The currency remains plagued by the risk of a policy easing and has now dropped some 6.0 percent since the Reserve Bank last cut official rates to 5.5 percent on May 23.

However, economists are not ruling out the possibility of a further easing, particularly as next week's key data are expected to show benign inflation and annual wages growth within the RBA's comfort zone.

"I'm not convinced that the economy has changed that much over past couple of weeks and that we are in recovery mode, and therefore we don't need to ease again," said Stephen Koukoulas, chief economist at Citibank Australia.
"A rate cut should still happen, but not too many of us are sure what weight the Reserve Bank is putting on the currency," he added.
The central bank did delay an easing by around a week after last December's board meeting due to a volatile local currency.

Last week's weaker than expected employment report had refuelled thoughts of a rate cut and had seen September bills touch a contract of 94.99 as the market fully priced in a further 50 basis points rate cut.

Meanwhile, Westpac's July consumer sentiment survey at 2.30 p.m. (0430 GMT) may generate more interest than usual given the current lack of data and as recent weakness in the series has added to calls for another rate cut.

The local yield curve continued to flatten as the short-end came under pressure, breaching support at 75 basis points on the 3/10 futures spread. Three-year yields also underperformed U.S. and Canada, but N.Z. yields rose more to firm up monetary conditions as the N.Z. dollar weakened.
